newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen heading lower next week.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen heading lower next week.

text.p: The Thai stock market, at over three-year-lows on the dumping by foreign funds of blue chip stocks, especially banks, could head still lower next week on lack of fresh, positive news, analysts said on Friday.

"I think we can expect a similar performance as this week," said Pattera Dilokrungthirapop, head of research at Crosby Securities, "I think we may see the market dribble down. It's definitely cheap but there is no real positive news set to drive the market up."
The market has fallen 15 percent since October 1.

She said even if expected third quarter profit figures from the banks and finance sector were better than expected they were unlikely to lift sentiment. This was because investors remained concerned about asset quality.
Pattera expected daily volumes would average a moderate four to five billion baht next week.

"Interest rate sensitive sectors, finance, property and banks are going to look weak again," said another analyst, "I don't see any real support. There is concern surrounding third quarter results and (bank and finance firm) loan exposure."
Although research analysts acknowledged sentiment remains poor they said selected stocks were beginning to look attractive.

"The key to this is sentiment and there isn't much positive news out there ... Some of the big banks, which came in for heavy selling this week are starting to look good value," said Mike Stead, Head of Research at Union Securities.
Jim Landi, reseach director at Nithipat Capital said: "Though we could see small sucessive falls. I think the support fund will keep coming in at around 900."
Money from a 15.7 billion baht (US$628 million) rescue fund operated by bankers and brokers has been in and out of the market since earlier this week and curbed steep falls.
Landi said there was long term value in high quality construction, electronic and bank stocks.
Traders said sentiment last week was hit by a 60 point, or 6.00 percent fall last Monday.
The Thai stock market has been battered since late last week because foreign funds have been underweighting Thailand stocks and moving into equities in other regional markets, analysts said.
They were worried about a slowing Thai economy and uncertainty about what type of a new government will emerge after general elections on November 17, they added.
